1. (Currently amended) An apparatus for aligning document actions specified in a documented procedure with demonstrated user actions, comprising: an alignment device comprising a processor and memory, the alignment device configured to compute an alignment between the document actions and the demonstrated user actions based on at least one similarity metric, wherein the alignment device performs a non-routine technological function beyond conventional computer operation by dynamically matching sequences of user-performed actions to procedural steps in real-time based on multi-modal input analysis.

2. (Currently amended) The apparatus of claim 1, wherein said alignment device identifies a current step in the documented procedure based on the alignment, and wherein the identification of the current step requires analysis of temporal sequences and action context not determinable through routine data processing.

3. (Currently amended) The apparatus of claim 2, wherein the documented procedure is displayed on a user interface, and said alignment device provides an identification of the current step to the user interface for use in highlighting the current step on the user interface, wherein the highlighting is dynamically updated based on real-time alignment computation.

4. (Currently amended) The apparatus of claim 2, further comprising a user interface, in signal communication with said alignment device, for displaying the documented procedure, and wherein said alignment device outputs an identification of the current step to the user interface, and said user interface highlights the current step based on the identification, wherein the alignment device continuously monitors demonstrated user actions and updates the highlighted current step without user intervention.

5. (Currently amended) The apparatus of claim 1, wherein said alignment device identifies a next step in the documented procedure based on the alignment, and wherein the identification of the next step requires predictive analysis of user intent based on partial action sequences.

6. (Currently amended) The apparatus of claim 5, wherein the documented procedure is displayed on a user interface, and said alignment device provides an identification of the next step to the user interface for use in highlighting the next step on the user interface, wherein the next step identification is computed before the user completes the current step.

7. (Currently amended) The apparatus of claim 5, further comprising a user interface, in signal communication with said alignment device, for displaying the documented procedure, and wherein said alignment device outputs an identification of the next step to the user interface, and said user interface highlights the next step based on the identification, wherein the user interface provides prospective guidance by highlighting anticipated next steps during execution of current steps.

9. (Currently amended) The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the demonstrated user actions are performed with respect to a user interface, and the at least one similarity metric is based on common strings in the user interface and the documented procedure, and wherein the similarity metric further incorporates contextual weighting based on action sequence position and temporal relationships.

10. (Currently amended) The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a camera, connected in signal communication with said alignment device, for capturing images of at least some of the demonstrated user actions, and wherein said alignment device uses at least some of the captured images to calculate the alignment by performing computer vision analysis to extract action parameters not available through conventional input monitoring.

11. (Currently amended) The apparatus of claim 1, wherein said alignment device computes the alignment further based on previous user experiences with respect to performing the documented procedure, and wherein the alignment computation incorporates machine learning models trained on historical action sequences to improve alignment accuracy over time.

12. (Currently amended) The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the documented procedure has a plurality of steps specified therein, and the apparatus further comprises a document action extractor for extracting at least some of the plurality of steps, wherein the document action extractor parses procedural documentation using natural language processing to identify discrete actionable steps.

13. (Currently amended) An apparatus for guiding user actions with respect to a documented procedure displayed on a user interface, the documented procedure having a plurality of steps specified therein, the apparatus comprising: an alignment device comprising a processor and memory, the alignment device configured to compute an alignment between the document actions and the demonstrated user actions based on at least one similarity metric, wherein the alignment computation performs a non-routine technological function by dynamically matching user actions to procedural steps in real-time; a highlighting device, connected in signal communication with said alignment device, for visually highlighting on the user interface at least a portion of a step in the documented procedure based on the alignment computed by said alignment device, wherein highlighting is updated continuously during user action execution; and a scrolling device, connected in signal communication with said alignment device, for automatically scrolling through each of the plurality of steps of the documented procedure on the user interface based on the alignment computed by said alignment device, wherein scrolling is triggered by alignment state transitions rather than manual user control.

15. (Currently amended) The apparatus of claim 13, further comprising a camera, connected in signal communication with said alignment device, for capturing images of at least some of the demonstrated user actions, and wherein said alignment device uses at least some of the captured images to calculate the alignment by performing computer vision analysis to extract action parameters.

16. (Currently amended) The apparatus of claim 13, wherein said alignment device computes the alignment further based on previous user experiences with respect to performing the documented procedure, and wherein the alignment computation incorporates machine learning models trained on historical action sequences.

17. (Currently amended) A method for aligning document actions specified in a documented procedure with demonstrated user actions, comprising the steps of: computing an alignment between the document actions and the demonstrated user actions based on at least one similarity metric, wherein the computing step includes analyzing temporal sequences and action context to determine alignment states, and wherein the alignment computation is performed continuously during user action execution rather than post-hoc analysis.

18. (Currently amended) The method of claim 17, further comprising the step of identifying a current step in the documented procedure based on the alignment, wherein the identification requires real-time analysis of action sequences and contextual information.

19. (Currently amended) The method of claim 18, wherein the documented procedure is displayed on a user interface, and the method further comprises the step of providing an identification of the current step to the user interface for use in highlighting the current step on the user interface, wherein the highlighting is updated dynamically during user action execution.

20. (Currently amended) The method of claim 17, further comprising the step of identifying a next step in the documented procedure based on the alignment, wherein the identification of the next step requires predictive analysis of user intent based on partial action sequences.

21. (Currently amended) The method of claim 20, wherein the documented procedure is displayed on a user interface, and the method further comprises the step of providing an identification of the next step to the user interface for use in highlighting the next step on the user interface, wherein the next step is identified and highlighted before completion of the current step.

23. (Currently amended) The method of claim 17, wherein the demonstrated user actions are performed with respect to a user interface, and the at least one similarity metric is based on common strings in the user interface and the documented procedure, and wherein the similarity metric further incorporates contextual weighting based on action sequence position.

24. (Currently amended) The method of claim 17, wherein said computing step computes the alignment based on images of at least some of the demonstrated user actions captured by an imaging device, wherein the computing step performs computer vision analysis to extract action parameters from the images.

25. (Currently amended) The method of claim 17, wherein said computing step computes the alignment further based on previous user experiences with respect to performing the documented procedure, and wherein the computing step incorporates machine learning models trained on historical action sequences.

26. (Currently amended) The method of claim 17, wherein the documented procedure has a plurality of steps specified therein, and the method further comprises the step of extracting at least some of the plurality of steps from the documented procedure, wherein the extracting step uses natural language processing to identify discrete actionable steps.

27. (Currently amended) A program storage device readable by machine, tangibly embodying a program of instructions executable by the machine to perform method steps for aligning document actions specified in a documented procedure with demonstrated user actions as recited in claim 17, wherein the program instructions, when executed, cause the machine to perform non-routine technological functions including real-time action sequence analysis and dynamic alignment computation.

28. (Currently amended) A method for guiding user actions with respect to a documented procedure displayed on a user interface, the documented procedure having a plurality of steps specified therein, the method comprising the steps of: computing an alignment between the document actions and the demonstrated user actions based on at least one similarity metric, wherein the computing step analyzes temporal sequences and action context in real-time; visually highlighting on the user interface at least a portion of a step in the documented procedure based on the computed alignment, wherein highlighting is updated continuously during user action execution; and automatically scrolling through each of the plurality of steps of the documented procedure on the user interface based on the computed alignment, wherein scrolling is triggered by alignment state transitions rather than manual user control.

30. (Currently amended) The method of claim 28, wherein said computing step computes the alignment based on images of at least some of the demonstrated user actions captured by an imaging device, wherein the computing step performs computer vision analysis to extract action parameters from the images.

31. (Currently amended) The method of claim 28, wherein said computing step computes the alignment further based on previous user experiences with respect to performing the documented procedure, and wherein the computing step incorporates machine learning models trained on historical action sequences.

32. (Currently amended) A program storage device readable by machine, tangibly embodying a program of instructions executable by the machine to perform method steps for guiding user actions with respect to a documented procedure displayed on a user interface as recited in claim 28, wherein the program instructions, when executed, cause the machine to perform non-routine technological functions including real-time alignment computation and dynamic interface updates.
